text:
maria: quick heads-up — after the kernel patch rolled yesterday we see a small but consistent p99 tail bump on hosted generation routes, ~120ms increase, not across-the-board but concentrated on long-seq with low kv-hit.

sam: saw the alert. timeline matches the kernel switch + continuous-batcher tweak. KV hit rate dropped ~5–7% in the same windows.

jia: do we have a flame or trace? paste what you have

maria: copy of the trace snippet (raw):
```
span: batch_assemble -> 412ms
span: kernel_select -> 8ms (prefers fused-attn-wav2)
span: kv_fetch -> 62ms (fallthrough miss)
span: token_gen -> 220ms
```

maria: interesting bit: batch_assemble step increased variance; we changed the batch formation heuristic to prefer larger microbatches for latency SLOs

rik: sounds like batch shape changed and broke prefetch locality. If batcher coalesces heterogeneous seq lengths we might be evicting useful KV entries.

sam: yep — current continuous-batcher uses token_budget_target=1024 and a max_wait_ms=12. That favours larger batches but increases interleaving.

jia: possible mitigations: 1) lower token_budget_target for long-seq lanes, 2) add kv-prefetch affinity so requests from same client are clustered, 3) introduce soft admit thresholds that probabilistically shed heavy sequences when kv-miss rate spikes.

maria: +1 to targeted token budget. Also saw a spike in queue depth before the tail; not steady overload, more like micro-bursts.

infra-bot: deploy completed: patch/continuous-batcher@rollout v2 -> us-west-2, 2025-06-02T08:17:03Z

sam: propose an experiment: A/B 10% traffic: a) token_budget_target=768 + max_wait_ms=8, kv_prefetch_window=3, b) current baseline. Monitor p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, backend GPU util.

jia: add a soft-429 backpressure probe: when queue_len > 140 for >50ms, prob_shed=10% (soft 429) for new arrivals that are > token_len 512. That should deflate tail without hard rejects.

maria: can we also log kernel selection counts per batch shape? want to see if kernel choice is oscillating causing cache churn.

ik: I'll add extra labels on the metrics pipeline: batch_shape, chosen_kernel, kv_hit_rate_before/after. Also add an A/B tag for the probe.

rik: FYI prefer probabilistic shed rather than deterministic to avoid oscillations.

sam: owner list: rik -> implement shed probe, ik -> metrics labels, maria -> run the traffic cut and monitor, jia -> guard eval set for quality regressions.

maria: timeline: start A/B tomorrow 09:30 PT, 1 hour ramp, 3 hours steady, quick rollback plan on any >10% p99 delta.

jia: add an alert for kv-hit drop >4% and p99 up >80ms for the A cohort.

maria: noted. I'll post the experiment link to the perf dashboard once it's provisioned: https://dash.redwood/perf/exp/1754321000

sam: one more: if the shed probe reduces cost but degrades quality, we can fall back to kernel pinning by seq-length to restore prefetch locality.

rik: ok I'll open a PR with flags and default opt-outs. tagging @eng-oncall for visibility.

maria: thanks — will collect logs and reconvene after steady window. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for exp-A (10% traffic) at 2025-06-03T16:30:00Z

maria: initial 10min check: p99 diff +5ms, kv-hit -3%, no quality regressions observed on eval set. continuing.
